name: Thonburi Kingdom
native: อาณาจักรธนบุรี
กรุงธนบุรี

predecessors.name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
predecessors.text: Ayutthaya and the Chao Phraya basin, which Taksin retook from the Burmese in November 1767

successors.name: Rattanakosin Kingdom (Siam)
successors.text: the whole Thonburi shape, held by Chakri as Rama I from April 1782

rulers.name: Taksin (Phraya Tak, King Taksin the Great)

ledger.x: 28 December 1767: Taksin is crowned at Thonburi.
1768: Thonburi conquers Phimai.
1769: Pattani sends tribute.
1769: Taksin presses Cambodia for tribute and invades 'that year without success'; the real invasion comes in 1771.
21 September 1769: Taksin captures Nakhon Si Thammarat.
8 August 1770: Taksin retakes Phitsanulok.
November 1771: the Siamese take Hà Tiên.
1773: the Siamese leave Cambodia and Hà Tiên.
1773: the Siamese leave Cambodia; Ang Ton abdicated in favour of Ang Non in 1775 and Ang Non was murdered in 1779.
1775: Nan comes under Thonburi's power ('Nan also came under its power that year').
January 1775: Thonburi takes Lampang and Lamphun from the Burmese.
15 January 1775: Chiang Mai is taken from the Burmese and made a Siamese tributary.
October 1775: the Burmese invade northern Siam.
1776: the Malay north stops obeying.
August 1776: the Burmese leave Siam.
1778: Luang Prabang is a Siamese vassal.
1778: Surasi captures Champasak.
1779: the occupation of Champasak ends.
March 1779: Vientiane falls and becomes a Siamese dependency.
1 April 1782: Taksin is deposed and Chakri becomes Rama I.

wars.name: Taksin's reconquest of Siam
wars.outcome: Taksin took Chanthaburi (June 1767), Ayutthaya-Thonburi (November 1767), Phimai (1768), Nakhon Si Thammarat (21 September 1769) and Phitsanulok (8 August 1770); 'Taksin's position was secured after the last rival fell'.

wars.name: Siamese invasions of Cambodia and Hà Tiên
wars.outcome: A failed invasion in 1769; Hà Tiên fell in November 1771 and Ang Non was installed in Cambodia; Vietnamese forces took Phnom Penh in July 1772 and the Siamese withdrew in 1773.

wars.name: Thonburi's Burmese wars (1771-1776)
wars.outcome: Burmese raids on Sawankhalok (1771) and Phichai (1772-1773), the Burmese defeat at Bangkaeo (March 1775) and the Siamese capture of Chiang Mai (15 January 1775); the Burmese took Sukhothai and Phitsanulok in 1775-1776 and left by August 1776.

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Lan Na (1774-1775)
wars.outcome: Chiang Mai was taken on 15 January 1775 with the help of Kawila of Lampang; Lan Na became a Thonburi tributary under Phaya Chaban; Chiang Mai was abandoned after a Burmese attack in 1777.

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Laos (1777-1779)
wars.outcome: Surasi captured Champasak in 1778; Vientiane fell in March 1779 and became a Siamese dependency; Luang Prabang is a Siamese vassal from 1778 (its own page).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line: Siam's frontiers with Burma, the Malay sultanates, Cambodia and the Lao kingdoms are approximate and the tributaries are tints.
